Custom Parts

Custom plastic parts: PTFE, POM, PE and acrylic

Guide strips, gears, transparent components and PTFE forms for custom plastic-part enquiries.

Study sections
PTFE components: small forms and stepped shafts
POM gears: define the tooth and hub details
PE guide strips: straight and curved profiles
Acrylic components: shape and viewing surfaces

These photographs and clips come from the supplied LZZ material collection.

Photography & project scope
Discuss your drawing
PTFE components: small forms and stepped shafts

The PTFE source collection brings together white components with holes, repeated intermediate forms and long stepped parts. These photographs show several geometries, rather than one assembly. For a similar inquiry, specify the exact material grade, the mating features and the dimensions that control fit.

Original part photographs
Small white components with holes, from the PTFE source collection.
Repeated intermediate forms arranged on a work surface; source labeled as PTFE semi-finished parts.
Long stepped components from the PTFE source collection.
PTFE part forms in the workshop

The clip shows white components arranged on a dark work surface, including round bases with projecting features. The source file identifies the group as PTFE parts.

18-second original clip

Select play to view the original footage.
POM gears: define the tooth and hub details

The gear clip shows a white toothed component with a raised hub and central bore, alongside other gear forms. For your own gear, provide the tooth specification, bore and hub dimensions, mating information and acceptance requirements. The source material identifies POM; the exact grade needs to be stated in the order.

A closer look at the POM gear

A person holds a white gear to show its teeth, hub and central opening. The clip provides a view of the part form, without a dimensional inspection result.

6-second original clip

Select play to view the original footage.
PE guide strips: straight and curved profiles

The PE clip shows green strips with straight and curved profiles. A guide-strip drawing should describe the cross-section, length or curved path, mounting features and interfaces. Identify any controlled sliding surface and agree its dimensional and surface requirements.

PE guide-strip examples

The original clip shows a group of green straight and curved strips on the workshop floor. Material identification follows the PE source label.

7-second original clip

Select play to view the original footage.
Acrylic components: shape and viewing surfaces

The photographs show transparent circular components with visible rims and stepped sections. The separate video shows a clear rectangular part with circular features and holes. Mark viewing surfaces, cosmetic limits and handling requirements alongside the dimensional drawing; sample appearance alone does not define an optical specification.

Original part photographs
Transparent circular components grouped together.
A closer view of the transparent rims and stepped forms.
Transparent acrylic part details

A clear rectangular component is held in front of the machine, showing circular recesses, holes and machined features from an oblique angle.

7-second original clip

Select play to view the original footage.
Plan a similar part

Send a 3D model and a revision-controlled drawing, material grade and quantity. Mark critical dimensions, mating features, edge conditions and appearance requirements. Agree the inspection records and packaging needs with your quotation.
